sentences.text: By the impugned judgment dated 30th January, 2024, the learned Trial Court has found the Appellant guilty of aggravated penetrative sexual assault under Section 6 of POCSO Act.
The Court holds that the victim was aged about 17 years at the time of the incident and the prosecution has proved its case for conviction.

The sentence awarded to the Appellant is as under:
"33.

In view of the above discussion, I conclude that there are no substantial and compelling circumstances justifying this court to deviate from the sentence of life imprisonment as prescribed by the legislation.
"Life sentence" would serve the interest of justice as well of the society.

Further, it will also not destroy the convict,
though it will serve as a general deterrence. 34(i).

Therefore, considering the overall conspectus of the case, this court is of the view that ends of justice would be met if the convict 'SV' is sentenced under section 6 POCSO Act (and not under section 376 IPC as punishment under section 6 POCSO Act is greater in degree) to rigorous imprisonment for life which shall mean Imprisonment for the remainder of natural life of the convict 'SV' and to pay fine of Rs. 10,000/-.
No separate sentence is awarded to the convict for the offences punishable under sections 354A IPC and Section 12 POCSO Act as they were committed in the course of same transaction.
(ii). In the event of his failure to pay the fine amount, the convict shall further undergo simple imprisonment for a period of thirty days.
Imprisonment in default of fine shall run consecutively."

Ld. APP for the State points out that in this case the interim compensation has also not been released to the survivor and the Court has expressed considerable concern on the fact that the Counsellor did not make any attempts to properly contact and trace the survivor.

The relevant portion of the judgment is set out below:
"

(v), This court vide orders dated 05.01.2024, 16.02.2024, 20.02.2024 and 04.03.2024 requested the learned Secretary, DLSA, West District, Tis Hazari Courts to depute a trained Counselor/Psychologist to ensure adjustment and rehabilitation of the victim and her family and to ensure that education of the victim or her siblings is not disrupted and normal life is restored at the earliest.

sentences.text: However, as per the report received on 11.03.2024 from the DLSA, victim could not be contacted.

Relevant of report reads as under:
"I tried to contact the concerned victim through telephonically on dated 22.02.2024,
24.02.2024 and 27.02.2024 respectively, despite this concerned victim neither received the call nor call back.

Despite repeated calls, victim's mother did not receive S.V vs State on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105940521/

sentences.text: From the perusal of the above report, it appears that the Counselor has not made sincere efforts because there is nothing in the report to suggest that she visited the family.
7. A perusal of the judgment also shows that the survivor gave birth to a child whose DNA sampling was also confirmed to be matching with the Appellant.
Thus the Appellant has been held to be biological father of the victim/ survivor as well as of the baby born to the survivor - who is also his biological daughter.
8. Under such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that urgent steps need to be taken to trace the survivor and to pay the interim compensation to This is a digitally signed order.

pagination and bookmarks for perusal of this Court by the next date of hearing.
Let the paperbook for the same be also prepared.
Let the TCR be tagged along with the present appeal.
Learned Counsel for the parties may obtain the electronic record of the Court, including the TCR and the paper book, upon request from the Registry.
10. In addition, let the survivor be served through the concerned SHO.
11. The Secretary, DLSA shall file a report in regard to failure to pay the interim compensation to the survivor till date in this case.
12. The concerned Counsellor and the Member Secretary, DLSA shall appear before the Court on the next date of hearing.

13. List on 2nd September, 2024 on top of Board as item no. 1.
14.
